fullPassage:
[1번] Local elementary schools are invited to join us in celebrating the 25th anniversary of the city's subway system. We're asking elementary students to create a poster that will be displayed in our subways during the celebration. The theme of the poster should be "uniting communities." Be creative and show us what the subway means to you and your community. Each student may submit only one poster by September 22. This event is less about competition than it is about showcasing community spirit. However, the winner will receive a special subway tour, and the winner's school will receive $500. There will also be a promotional photoshoot featuring the winner and all of the winner's classmates. The judging period will take no longer than one week. So we expect to announce a winner by October 1. We hope everyone participates!

[2번] Have you ever walked through a city on a windy day? If you have, you probably noticed that the wind was stronger near tall buildings. This is called the "downdraught effect." Generally, the higher you go, the stronger the winds are. When strong winds high above the ground hit a tall building, they can't go through it. Instead, they go up, down, or around the sides of the building. The wind that shoots down to the ground is strong at street level. Having several tall buildings near one another can also increase wind speeds. This is due to the "channeling effect," which occurs when the wind blows through the narrow spaces between the buildings. It's similar to water flowing in a river — the narrower the space, the faster it moves.

[3번] Hoarding disorder is a mental illness characterized by the inability to get rid of possessions that have no use or value. It is often accompanied by "excessive acquisition," which means sufferers feel the need to own as many things as possible. Hoarding behavior tends to start at an early age and becomes more and more extreme as the person grows older. Once it becomes a significant problem, it is generally treated with behavioral therapy, which helps hoarders make better decisions about keeping or getting rid of their belongings. However, as hoarding disorder can be a complex condition with multiple causes, this treatment often takes a long time, and additional methods may be required.

[4번] Have you ever seen rows of identical fruit or vegetables in the supermarket? They may look pretty, but consider this — perfectly fine produce that looks a little different is being wasted. In fact, some farmers end up throwing away as much as 50 percent of their harvest because it doesn't look quite right. Fortunately, this is beginning to change. All of this wasted produce tastes just as good as what they sell in the supermarket. So there are now some organizations that buy ugly produce from farmers and sell it to consumers at prices as much as 30 percent lower than normal. Not only does this practice benefit farmers and consumers, but it also helps protect the environment, since farmers don't have to waste resources growing unwanted produce.

[5번] Palm scanning is a form of biometrics that uses the palm of a person's hand as a unique form of identification. More specifically, it maps the vein patterns that are found in the person's palm. After the scan is complete, it compares the patterns to existing scans to look for matches. If there are no matches, it is added to the database. Once recorded and stored, these palm scans can serve as a person's digital signature for both online and in-person transactions. As a result, people no longer need to carry credit cards or cash. Soon, people may be able to make purchases with just their hand. Furthermore, there is little chance of fraud. No biometric system is harder to fool than palm scans. Vein patterns are unique, and unlike fingerprints, cannot easily be taken without a person's knowledge. This guarantees a level of safety greater than that of any other system.

[6번] It is now believed that deserts may be perfect places for harvesting solar power. If this is true, there would be no other place as ideal as the Sahara, the world's largest desert. Unfortunately, solar farms in the desert could have adverse environmental effects. For example, covering half the Sahara with solar farms would raise local temperatures by approximately 2.5 °C. This warming would not be limited to the desert — it would spread around the globe, eventually increasing the world's average temperature by 0.39 °C. This could speed up global warming by melting sea ice and exposing the dark water beneath it, which absorbs greater amounts of solar energy than sea ice does. Rising temperatures in the Sahara could also cause other problems by changing global precipitation patterns, including droughts in the Amazon and more frequent tropical cyclones.

[7번] Research suggests that when we use the term "brilliant," we usually apply it to men rather than women. It is said that this is an unconscious bias that occurs all across the world. It may also be the reason why even brilliant women are less likely to be employed in fields where a high level of intelligence is prized, such as math and science. A study conducted in 2016 analyzed 14 million student reviews of university faculty members. It found that male professors were two to three times more likely to be described with the words "brilliant" or "genius" than female professors were. Furthermore, students were more likely to use these words in reference to professors of physics and philosophy, two fields with relatively few women. These results suggest that we either underestimate women or overestimate men. This is why we need to be aware of the words we use and think about why we use them.

[8번] Coral reefs are being threatened by unusually warm water that is causing them to bleach and die. One team of researchers has devised an unusual plan to deal with this. They intend to record the sounds of healthy reefs and then play them near reefs that are suffering from severe bleaching. A healthy reef is noisy, and it is believed that this attracts young fish, letting them know that this is a place where they can safely live. Damaged reefs, on the contrary, are silent. They attract few new inhabitants, which causes them to degrade even further. The researchers tested their idea at a reef severely affected by bleaching. Healthy reef sounds were played in certain locations for 40 days. At the end of this period, the researchers found that the areas where the sounds were played had attracted twice as many young fish as places that were left silent.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: announcing → announce (expect to 뒤 to부정사이므로 동사원형)
det.analysis:
① displayed: 'will be __________'는 수동태라 과거분사 displayed가 맞아요 — 적절
② submit: 'may __________ only one poster'에서 조동사 may 뒤에는 동사원형 submit이 와야 해요 — 적절
③ featuring: 'a photoshoot __________ the winner'를 꾸미는 분사(-ing)라 featuring이 맞아요 — 적절
④ announcing: 'we expect to __________'에서 to부정사 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 해요. 그래서 announcing(-ing)이 아니라 announce가 맞아요. ←정답
det.tip: expect to + 동사원형 → to announce. to announcing은 틀림

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: high up in the clouds=구름 높이 / far out at sea=먼 바다에서 / at street level=거리(지면) 높이에서 / near the mountain top=산꼭대기 근처에서
det.analysis:
① high up in the clouds: 구름 높이? 바람은 땅으로 내려온다는 흐름과 반대
② far out at sea: 먼 바다? 도시 이야기와 무관
③ at street level: 땅으로 내리꽂힌 바람이 거리(지면) 높이에서 세게 느껴짐 ←정답
④ near the mountain top: 산꼭대기? 본문 무관
det.tip: The wind that shoots down to the ground is strong ___ → at street level(거리 높이)

questions.passage: Hoarding disorder ①<u>makes</u> it very hard for a person to throw away old things. Because these useless items ②<u>keep</u> piling up, the home slowly fills with objects that ③<u>have</u> little value. With steady support over time, many patients ④<u>learns</u> to decide what they should keep.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.

det.korean: learns → learn (주어 many patients가 복수이므로 동사도 복수형 learn)
det.analysis:
① makes: 주어 'Hoarding disorder'가 단수라 3인칭 단수 makes — 적절해요.
② keep: 주어 'these useless items'가 복수라 복수 동사 keep — 적절해요.
③ have: 'objects that have little value'에서 선행사 objects가 복수라 복수 동사 have — 적절해요.
④ learns: 주어 'many patients'가 복수이므로 동사도 복수형 learn이어야 해요. 3인칭 단수형 learns는 틀립니다 ←정답
det.tip: 복수 주어(many patients)에는 -s 없는 동사원형 → learn

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: are being → is being (주어 produce는 단수라 is)
det.analysis:
① are being: 'perfectly fine produce that looks a little different ___ wasted'에서 진짜 주어는 produce(농산물)로 단수예요. 중간에 관계절(that looks ~)이 끼어 헷갈리지만 동사는 단수 is여야 해요. 그래서 is being이 맞고 are being은 틀림 ←정답

② buy: 관계대명사 that의 선행사 organizations(복수)라 buy — 적절

③ does this: 부정어 Not only 도치 구문의 does — 적절

det.tip: 주어 produce(단수) + 관계절 → 동사는 단수 is being wasted

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: little chance of fraud=사기 가능성이 거의 없음. 뒤의 '속이기 가장 어렵다'가 근거
det.analysis:
빈칸 뒤에 'No biometric system is harder to fool than palm scans(어떤 생체 시스템도 손바닥 스캔보다 속이기 어렵지 않다)'로 안전성을 강조해요.

④ a long waiting time(긴 대기 시간): 문맥 무관
det.tip: 속이기 가장 어려움 → 사기 가능성 거의 없음(little chance of fraud)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: beneficial → adverse ('Unfortunately' 뒤라 부정적 영향)
det.analysis:
① harvesting: 사막은 태양광을 수확하기 좋은 곳 — 적절
② beneficial: 'Unfortunately, solar farms ~ could have __________ environmental effects'에서 앞에 'Unfortunately(불행하게도)'가 있으므로 부정적인 adverse가 맞음. '이로운(beneficial)'은 모순이라 부적절 ←정답
③ melting: 해빙을 녹여 온난화를 가속 — 적절
④ frequent: 더 잦은 열대성 저기압 — 적절
det.tip: Unfortunately → adverse(부정적) effects. beneficial(이로운)은 정반대

questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ③ 'played in certain locations for 40 days' → 모든 지역이 아니라 특정 장소들 → 불일치
det.analysis:
① 건강한 산호초 소리를 녹음해 백화가 심한 산호초 근처에서 재생: 'record the sounds of healthy reefs and then play them near reefs suffering from severe bleaching'과 일치
② 안전하게 살 수 있는 곳임을 알림: 'letting them know that this is a place where they can safely live'와 일치
③ 40일 동안 '모든' 지역에서 재생됨? ←정답(불일치): 본문은 '특정 장소들에서(in certain locations)' 재생했다고 했어요. '모든 지역'이 아니라 일부 장소라서 진술이 본문과 어긋나요.
④ 손상된 산호초는 조용하며 서식 동물을 거의 못 끌어들임: 'Damaged reefs ... are silent. They attract few new inhabitants'와 일치
det.tip: in certain locations(특정 장소들) ≠ 모든 지역 → ③이 불일치

ch: 연구팀은 건강한 산호초의 소리를 녹음해 백화가 심한 산호초 근처에서 재생하려 한다.
건강한 산호초의 소리는 어린 물고기에게 안전하게 살 수 있는 곳임을 알린다.
실험에서 건강한 산호초의 소리는 40일 동안 모든 지역에서 재생되었다.
손상된 산호초는 조용하며 새로운 서식 동물을 거의 끌어들이지 못한다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ① stronger=더 센 ② hit=치다 ③ occurs=발생하다 ④ similar→different (부적절)

questions.passage: Have you ever ①<u>seen</u> rows of identical fruit or vegetables in the supermarket? They may look pretty, but consider this — perfectly fine produce that looks a little different is being wasted. In fact, some farmers end up ②<u>throw</u> away as much as 50 percent of their harvest because it doesn't look quite right. Fortunately, this is beginning to change. All of this wasted produce ③<u>tastes</u> just as good as what they sell in the supermarket. So there are now some organizations that buy ugly produce from farmers and sell it to consumers at prices as much as 30 percent lower than normal. Not only does this practice benefit farmers and consumers, but it also helps protect the environment, since farmers don't have to waste resources ④<u>growing</u> unwanted produce.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중 어법상 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: throw → throwing (end up 뒤에는 동명사 -ing)
det.analysis:
① seen: 'Have you ever seen ~' 현재완료(have + p.p.)의 seen — 적절

② throw: 'end up ___ away'에서 end up 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)가 와요. 그래서 throwing이 맞아요. 동사원형 throw는 틀림 ←정답

③ tastes: 주어 'All of this wasted produce(농산물)'는 단수 취급이라 단수동사 tastes — 적절

④ growing: 'waste resources growing ~' 자원을 낭비하며 재배하는 동시동작을 나타내는 분사 — 적절
det.tip: end up + V-ing(동명사) = 결국 ~하게 되다 → end up throwing away

questions.passage: Palm scanning is a form of biometrics that uses the palm of a person's hand as a unique form of identification. More specifically, it maps the vein patterns that are found in the person's palm. After the scan is complete, it compares the patterns to existing scans to look for matches. If there are no matches, it is added to the database. Once recorded and stored, these palm scans can serve as a person's digital signature for both online and in-person transactions. As a result, people no longer need to carry credit cards or cash. Soon, people may be able to make purchases with just their hand. Furthermore, there is little chance of fraud. No biometric system is harder to fool than palm scans. Vein patterns are unique, and unlike fingerprints, cannot easily be taken without a person's knowledge. This guarantees a level of safety greater than that of any other system.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ④가 본문(기존 스캔과 비교해 일치를 찾음)과 일치
det.analysis:
① 불일치 — 손바닥 스캔으로 '더는 신용카드가 필요 없다(no longer need)'고 했어요.
② 불일치 — 정맥 패턴은 '지문과 달리(unlike fingerprints)' 몰래 채취되기 어렵다고 했어요.
③ 불일치 — '일치하는 것이 없을 때(If there are no matches)' 새 스캔이 추가돼요. 일치가 있을 때가 아니에요.
④ 일치 — 'it compares the patterns to existing scans to look for matches(기존 스캔과 비교해 일치를 찾는다)'와 맞아요 ←정답
det.tip: 기존 스캔과 비교해 일치 확인 → ④ 일치

ch: 손바닥 스캔을 쓰려면 여전히 신용카드가 반드시 필요하다.
손바닥 스캔은 지문처럼 본인 모르게 쉽게 채취될 수 있다.
일치하는 패턴이 있을 때 새 스캔이 데이터베이스에 추가된다.
손바닥 스캔은 정맥 패턴을 기존 스캔과 비교해 일치 여부를 확인한다.

questions.passage: It is now believed that deserts may be perfect places for harvesting solar power. If this is true, there would be no other place as ideal as the Sahara, the world's largest desert. Unfortunately, solar farms in the desert could have adverse environmental effects. For example, covering half the Sahara with solar farms would raise local temperatures by approximately 2.5 °C. This warming would not be limited to the desert — it would spread around the globe, eventually increasing the world's average temperature by 0.39 °C. This could speed up global warming by melting sea ice and exposing the dark water beneath it, which absorbs greater amounts of solar energy than sea ice does. Rising temperatures in the Sahara could also cause other problems by changing global precipitation patterns, including droughts in the Amazon and more frequent tropical cyclones.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 핵심: 사막(사하라) 태양광 발전이 국지·지구 기온 상승과 강수 변화 등 부정적 환경 영향을 줄 수 있음
det.analysis:
① 사막 태양광 발전이 일으킬 수 있는 부정적 환경 영향: 국지 기온 상승 → 지구 온난화 가속 → 강수 패턴 변화까지 글 전체를 포괄 ←정답
② 건설 기술: 시설을 '짓는 기술'은 다루지 않음
③ 사막의 면적·기후 분포: 본문 소재가 아님
④ 경제적 이익: 본문에 없는 내용
det.tip: 사막 태양광의 부정적 환경 영향 = 글 전체 주제

ch: 사막 태양광 발전이 일으킬 수 있는 부정적 환경 영향
사하라 사막에 태양광 시설을 짓는 건설 기술
전 세계 사막의 면적과 기후 분포

questions.passage: Research suggests that when we use the term "brilliant," we usually apply it to men rather than women. It is said that this is an unconscious bias that occurs all across the world. It may also be the reason why even brilliant women are less likely to be employed in fields where a high level of intelligence is prized, such as math and science. A study conducted in 2016 analyzed 14 million student reviews of university faculty members. It found that male professors were two to three times more likely to be described with the words "brilliant" or "genius" than female professors were. Furthermore, students were more likely to use these words in reference to professors of physics and philosophy, two fields with relatively few women. These results suggest that we either underestimate women or overestimate men. This is why we need to be aware of the words we use and think about why we use them.
questions.stem: 사람들은 '뛰어난(brilliant)'이라는 말을 남성보다 여성에게 더 자주 쓰는 경향이 있다.

det.korean: 원문 S1 'we usually apply it to men rather than women' → 여성보다 남성에게 더 씀 → 뒤바뀜 → F
det.analysis: 본문은 '뛰어난'이라는 말을 여성보다 '남성에게(to men rather than women)' 더 자주 적용한다고 했어요. 진술은 남녀를 뒤바꿨으므로 사실과 반대 → F ←정답
det.tip: apply it to men rather than women — 남녀를 뒤바꾸면 불일치

questions.passage: Coral reefs are being threatened by unusually warm water that is causing them to bleach and die. One team of researchers has devised an unusual plan to deal with this. They intend to record the sounds of healthy reefs and then play them near reefs that are suffering from severe bleaching. A healthy reef is noisy, and it is believed that this attracts young fish, letting them know that this is a place where they can safely live. Damaged reefs, on the contrary, are silent. They attract few new inhabitants, which causes them to degrade even further. The researchers tested their idea at a reef severely affected by bleaching. Healthy reef sounds were played in certain locations for 40 days. At the end of this period, the researchers found that the areas where the sounds were played had attracted twice as many young fish as places that were left silent.
questions.stem: 위 글에서, 연구팀이 고안한 특이한 계획이 무엇에 '대처하기(맞서기)' 위한 것인지, '이것에 대처하다'라는 의미의 표현을 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오. (3단어, 영어로)

det.korean: deal with this = 이것에 대처하다
det.analysis: 본문 'One team of researchers has devised an unusual plan to deal with this'에서 연구팀은 '이것(산호초 백화 문제)에 대처하기(deal with this)' 위한 특이한 계획을 고안했어요. deal(동사) + with(전치사) + this(대명사) = 3단어예요.
det.tip: plan to deal with this = 이것에 대처하기 위한 계획

questions.passage: We're asking elementary students to create a poster that will be displayed in our subways during the __________ (celebrate). The theme of the poster should be "uniting communities."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: celebrate(동사: 기념하다) → celebration. 관사 the 뒤 전치사 during의 목적어 자리이므로 명사형
det.analysis: celebrate를 명사 celebration으로 변환. 'during the __________'에서 전치사 during과 관사 the 뒤에는 명사가 와야 하므로 명사형 celebration이 필요해요.
det.tip: during the __________ = 관사 뒤 명사 자리 → celebration

questions.passage: Have you ever walked through a city on a windy day? If you have, you probably noticed that the wind was stronger near tall buildings. This is called the "downdraught effect." Generally, the higher you go, the stronger the winds are. When strong winds high above the ground hit a tall building, they can't go through it. Instead, they go up, down, or around the sides of the building. The wind that shoots down to the ground is strong at street level. Having several tall buildings near one another can also increase wind speeds. This is due to the "channeling effect," which occurs when the wind blows through the narrow spaces between the buildings. It's similar to water flowing in a river — the narrower the space, the faster it moves.
questions.stem: 여러 개의 높은 건물이 가까이 있을 때 바람 속도를 높이는 효과를 본문에서 찾아 2단어로 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: channeling effect = 통로 효과
det.analysis: 본문 'Having several tall buildings near one another can also increase wind speeds. This is due to the "channeling effect"' — 여러 건물이 풍속을 높이는 효과 = channeling effect(통로 효과)
det.tip: several tall buildings → 풍속 증가 효과 = channeling effect

questions.passage: Once it becomes a significant problem, it is generally treated with behavioral therapy. As hoarding disorder can be a complex condition with multiple causes, this treatment often takes a long time, and additional methods may be __________ (require).
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: require(동사: 필요로 하다) → required (과거분사, 수동태: 필요로 되다). 'may be __________'는 조동사 + be + 과거분사의 수동태
det.analysis: 동사 require를 과거분사 required로 바꿔요. 'additional methods may be __________'에서 'may be' 뒤 빈칸은 수동태(조동사 + be + 과거분사)의 과거분사 자리예요. 추가적인 방법이 '필요로 되어질' 수 있다는 수동 의미라 required가 맞아요.
det.tip: may be + 과거분사 = 수동태 → may be required(필요로 될 수 있다)

They may look pretty, but consider this — perfectly fine produce that looks a little different is being wasted. In fact, some farmers end up throwing away as much as 50 percent of their harvest because it doesn't look quite right. Fortunately, this is beginning to change. All of this wasted produce tastes just as good as what they sell in the supermarket. So there are now some organizations that buy ugly produce from farmers and sell it to consumers at prices as much as 30 percent lower than normal. Not only does this practice benefit farmers and consumers, but it also helps protect the environment, since farmers don't have to waste resources growing unwanted produce.
questions.stem: 위 글에서, 일부 단체들이 농부에게서 무엇을 하는지를 나타내는 부분을, 동사 buy로 시작하여 본문에서 찾아 5단어로 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: buy ugly produce from farmers = 농부에게서 못난이 농산물을 사다
det.analysis: 본문 'some organizations that buy ugly produce from farmers'에서 단체들이 하는 일 = buy ugly produce from farmers(농부에게서 못난이 농산물을 사다). buy(사다) + ugly produce(못난이 농산물을) + from farmers(농부에게서). 5단어.
det.tip: buy + 목적어(ugly produce) + from + 출처(farmers)
